prompt: Find the exact value of $\cos 315^\circ$. Type it as an expression, for example "-sqrt(3)/2" for $-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $\cos 300^\circ$: the reference angle $60^\circ$ gives the size $\frac{1}{2}$, and Quadrant IV lies right of the $y$-axis, so cosine stays positive: $\frac{1}{2}$.
Now the sign. $315^\circ$ is in Quadrant IV — is the $x$-coordinate there positive or negative?
Quadrant IV is to the RIGHT of the $y$-axis, so $x$ is positive: $\cos 315^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

explanation: $315^\circ$ is in Quadrant IV, with reference angle $360^\circ - 315^\circ = 45^\circ$.
Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, and Quadrant IV lies to the right of the $y$-axis, so cosine stays POSITIVE: $\cos 315^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \approx 0.71$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the point
steps: At $315^\circ$ you are $45^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis, in the lower-right of the circle.
That point is $\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$: right of center (positive $x$) and below center (negative $y$).
Cosine reads the first coordinate, so it is positive.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap answer is $-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ — sticking a minus sign on the answer just because $315^\circ$ feels like a "far around the circle" angle.

Signs are not about how large the angle is; they are about direction. Ask the two questions separately: left or right of center (cosine), above or below center (sine). At $315^\circ$ you are to the RIGHT, so cosine is positive; only the sine is negative there.
